question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3
solution:
The correct answer is '**both**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage emphasizes that newspapers have the dual role of providing entertainment as well as information.
 
• The chosen term should reflect this dual role, indicating that newspapers serve simultaneously in both capacities.
 
• "**Both**" is appropriate as it indicates the presence of two qualities—entertainment and information—aligned with the passage context.
 
• Other options ("**either**", "**or**", "**nor**") do not fit because they do not accurately convey the dual nature of the function described.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

Complete Passage: *The newspaper is one of the significant signs of modern civilisation. It is the most popular form of reading in the present times because it interests all sorts of people. It is full of political news, sports and commercial news, as well as articles by well-known writers. A newspaper keeps us both entertained and informed. In these days of democracy, public opinion rules everywhere. No government can long withstand the pressure of a strong public opinion. It is, therefore, quite clear that the press controls public opinion, and public opinion, in turn, controls the government. Ultimately, the press controls the government. It acts as an interpreter between the government and the people and brings the rulers and the ruled together.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Either (या): "Either" is used to indicate one or the other of two choices, which does not fit the context of serving dual roles together.
 
• Or (या): "Or" indicates an alternative, which does not align with the dual function of newspapers providing entertainment and information together.
 
• Nor (और न ही): "Nor" is used to introduce a further negative statement, which is not appropriate in the context provided.
